(2) antilipschitz_measure_bound covers step 7 with facts (a)-(d). It says that Lⁿ(S) ≤ Kⁿ·Hⁿ(f(S)) whenever f is K-anti-Lipschitz on an arbitrary S ⊆ ℝⁿ.

subproblems.title: Injective strict derivative gives a local anti-Lipschitz bound
subproblems.statement: Let n, p ∈ ℕ and write ℝᵈ = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d) with the Euclidean norm |·|. Let Φ : ℝⁿ → ℝᵖ be any map, A : ℝⁿ → ℝᵖ a continuous linear map, and u₀ ∈ ℝⁿ. Suppose Φ has strict Fréchet derivative A at u₀ (HasStrictFDerivAt Φ A u₀), i.e. Φ(x) − Φ(y) − A(x − y) = o(|x − y|) as (x, y) → (u₀, u₀). Suppose also that A is injective. Then there are a neighbourhood s of u₀ and a constant K ∈ ℝ≥0 such that |x − y| ≤ K·|Φ(x) − Φ(y)| for all x, y ∈ s.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (n p : ℕ) (Φ : Rn n → Rn p) (A : Rn n →L[ℝ] Rn p) (u₀ : Rn n), HasStrictFDerivAt Φ A u₀ → Function.Injective A → ∃ s ∈ 𝓝 u₀, ∃ K : ℝ≥0, ∀ x ∈ s, ∀ y ∈ s, ‖x - y‖ ≤ K * ‖Φ x - Φ y‖
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source. Extracted from the parent proof of section3_chart_coordinateProjection_pos: step 4, the neighbourhood estimate of step 5 (HasStrictFDerivAt.approximates_deriv_on_nhds), and step 6. The parent follows Simon, Ch. 3, proof of Lemma 3.3, printed p. 79, where p_J restricted to N near x is used as a local C¹ diffeomorphism; the parent proof replaces the inverse function theorem by strict differentiability. Here the argument is stated for an arbitrary map Φ with strict derivative A.

Notation. ℝᵈ = Rn d = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d) with the Euclidean norm |·|. ℝ≥0 = [0, ∞).

Statement. Let n, p ∈ ℕ, Φ : ℝⁿ → ℝᵖ, A : ℝⁿ → ℝᵖ continuous linear and injective, and u₀ ∈ ℝⁿ. Suppose Φ has strict Fréchet derivative A at u₀ (HasStrictFDerivAt Φ A u₀). Then there are a neighbourhood s of u₀ and K ∈ ℝ≥0 with |x − y| ≤ K·|Φ(x) − Φ(y)| for all x, y ∈ s.

Proof.

1. Linear lower bound. A is linear and injective, so ker A = {0}. Since ℝⁿ is finite-dimensional, there is K₀ ∈ ℝ≥0 with K₀ > 0 such that |v − w| ≤ K₀·|Av − Aw| for all v, w ∈ ℝⁿ. By linearity, Av − Aw = A(v − w), so equivalently |v| ≤ K₀·|Av| for all v ∈ ℝⁿ.
Justification. If n = 0, then ℝ⁰ = {0} and K₀ := 1 works. If n ≥ 1, the unit sphere Σ := {v : |v| = 1} is nonempty and compact. The function v ↦ |Av| is continuous on Σ and, by injectivity, strictly positive there. So m := min over v ∈ Σ of |Av| satisfies m > 0. For v ≠ 0, |Av| = |v|·|A(v/|v|)| ≥ m·|v|, and the case v = 0 is trivial. Hence K₀ := 1/m works.
Mathlib: apply LinearMap.exists_antilipschitzWith to A as a linear map, using LinearMap.ker_eq_bot.mpr for injectivity. This gives K₀ > 0 with AntilipschitzWith K₀ A. Then AntilipschitzWith.le_mul_dist gives dist v w ≤ K₀·dist (A v) (A w), where dist is the norm of the difference.

2. Uniform linear approximation near u₀. Put c := (2K₀)⁻¹ ∈ ℝ≥0. Then c > 0 because K₀ > 0. Strict differentiability of Φ at u₀ with derivative A means Φ(x) − Φ(y) − A(x − y) = o(|x − y|) as (x, y) → (u₀, u₀). Hence there is a neighbourhood s of u₀ with |Φ(x) − Φ(y) − A(x − y)| ≤ c·|x − y| for all x, y ∈ s.
Mathlib: HasStrictFDerivAt.approximates_deriv_on_nhds with Or.inr (0 < c) gives s ∈ 𝓝 u₀ and ApproximatesLinearOn Φ A s c. This unfolds to exactly the displayed inequality for all x ∈ s and y ∈ s.

3. Triangle inequality. Fix x, y ∈ s. Since A(x − y) = (Φ(x) − Φ(y)) − (Φ(x) − Φ(y) − A(x − y)), the triangle inequality and step 2 give
|A(x − y)| ≤ |Φ(x) − Φ(y)| + |Φ(x) − Φ(y) − A(x − y)| ≤ |Φ(x) − Φ(y)| + c·|x − y|.

4. Combination. Apply step 1 with v = x − y, then multiply step 3 by K₀ ≥ 0:
|x − y| ≤ K₀·|A(x − y)| ≤ K₀·|Φ(x) − Φ(y)| + K₀·c·|x − y| = K₀·|Φ(x) − Φ(y)| + |x − y|/2.
The last equality holds because K₀·c = K₀/(2K₀) = 1/2, using K₀ > 0.

5. Conclusion. Subtract the real number |x − y|/2 from both sides: |x − y|/2 ≤ K₀·|Φ(x) − Φ(y)|, i.e. |x − y| ≤ 2K₀·|Φ(x) − Φ(y)|. So the neighbourhood s of u₀ and K := 2K₀ ∈ ℝ≥0 satisfy |x − y| ≤ K·|Φ(x) − Φ(y)| for all x, y ∈ s. ∎

Remark. Only strict differentiability at the single point u₀ is used. The case n = 0 is included: then |x − y| = 0 and the inequality is trivial.
proof_key_steps: Injectivity of the linear map A on finite-dimensional ℝⁿ gives K₀ > 0 with |v| ≤ K₀|Av| for all v (LinearMap.exists_antilipschitzWith).
Strict differentiability gives a neighbourhood s of u₀ with |Φx − Φy − A(x − y)| ≤ (2K₀)⁻¹|x − y| for x, y ∈ s (HasStrictFDerivAt.approximates_deriv_on_nhds).
By the triangle inequality, |A(x − y)| ≤ |Φx − Φy| + (2K₀)⁻¹|x − y| on s.
Combining gives |x − y| ≤ K₀|Φx − Φy| + |x − y|/2, hence |x − y| ≤ 2K₀|Φx − Φy|; take K = 2K₀.

subproblems.title: Anti-Lipschitz maps on subsets of ℝⁿ satisfy Lⁿ(S) ≤ Kⁿ·Hⁿ(f(S))
subproblems.statement: Let n, p ∈ ℕ and write ℝᵈ = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d) with the Euclidean norm |·|. Let f : ℝⁿ → ℝᵖ be any map, S ⊆ ℝⁿ an arbitrary set (not assumed measurable), and K ∈ ℝ≥0 such that |x − y| ≤ K·|f(x) − f(y)| for all x, y ∈ S. Then Lⁿ(S) ≤ Kⁿ·Hⁿ(f(S)) in [0, ∞]. Here Lⁿ = volume is Lebesgue outer measure on ℝⁿ, and Hⁿ = μHE[n] is the Euclidean-normalised n-dimensional Hausdorff outer measure on ℝᵖ.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (n p : ℕ) (f : Rn n → Rn p) (S : Set (Rn n)) (K : ℝ≥0), (∀ x ∈ S, ∀ y ∈ S, ‖x - y‖ ≤ K * ‖f x - f y‖) → volume S ≤ (K : ℝ≥0∞) ^ n * μHE[n] (f '' S)
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source. Extracted from the parent proof of section3_chart_coordinateProjection_pos, step 7 with its facts (a)-(d). The parent follows Simon, Ch. 3, proof of Lemma 3.3, printed p. 79: “... is a C¹ diffeomorphism onto an open W ... and so Hⁿ(p_{j₁,…,jₙ}(S ∩ N ∩ B_ρ(x))) > 0”. Here the argument is stated for an arbitrary map f and an arbitrary set S.

Notation. ℝᵈ = Rn d = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d) with the Euclidean norm |·|. For a metric space X with its Borel σ-algebra and d ≥ 0, μH[d] is the d-dimensional Hausdorff measure of X (Mathlib hausdorffMeasure). Hⁿ = μHE[n] is its Euclidean normalisation, and Lⁿ = volume on ℝⁿ. All of these are evaluated on arbitrary sets as outer measures. All values lie in [0, ∞], where multiplication is commutative, associative and monotone in each argument.

Statement. Let n, p ∈ ℕ, f : ℝⁿ → ℝᵖ, S ⊆ ℝⁿ an arbitrary set (no measurability assumed), and K ∈ ℝ≥0. Suppose |x − y| ≤ K·|f(x) − f(y)| for all x, y ∈ S. Then Lⁿ(S) ≤ Kⁿ·Hⁿ(f(S)).

Proof.

1. Facts.
(a) For every metric space X, μHE[n] = c_n·μH[n] as measures on X. Here c_n := addHaarScalarFactor(volume on ℝⁿ, μH[n]) ∈ ℝ≥0 is a single constant, independent of X. This is the definition (Mathlib MeasureTheory.Measure.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_def). Evaluated on a set E, it gives μHE[n](E) = c_n·μH[n](E) (Measure.smul_apply).
(b) On ℝⁿ, μHE[n] = Lⁿ (Mathlib EuclideanSpace.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_eq_volume).
(c) Let g : X → Y be a map between metric spaces and K ∈ ℝ≥0 with dist(a, b) ≤ K·dist(g(a), g(b)) for all a, b ∈ X. Then μH[d](E) ≤ K^d·μH[d](g(E)) for every d ≥ 0 and every E ⊆ X.
Mathlib: AntilipschitzWith.le_hausdorffMeasure_image. Its hypothesis AntilipschitzWith K g follows from the displayed inequality by AntilipschitzWith.of_le_mul_dist.
(d) If ι : Z → W is an isometry and d ≥ 0, then μH[d](ι(E)) = μH[d](E) for every E ⊆ Z (Mathlib Isometry.hausdorffMeasure_image, with side condition 0 ≤ d). The inclusion ι : S → ℝⁿ, with S carrying its subspace metric, is an isometry (isometry_subtype_coe).

2. The restricted map is anti-Lipschitz. Give S the subspace metric dist_S(a, b) = |a − b|, and let g : S → ℝᵖ, g(a) := f(a) (Set.domRestrict). For a, b ∈ S the hypothesis reads
dist_S(a, b) = |a − b| ≤ K·|f(a) − f(b)| = K·dist(g(a), g(b)).
So fact (c) applies to g with this K.

3. Hausdorff estimate inside S. Apply (c) to g with d := n ≥ 0 and E := S (the whole space S):
μH[n]_S(S) ≤ Kⁿ·μH[n]_{ℝᵖ}(g(S)), and g(S) = f(S).
In (c) the power K^d has the real exponent d = n, and it equals the natural power Kⁿ (ENNReal.rpow_natCast).

4. Transfer to ℝⁿ. Apply (d) to ι with E := S (the whole space S). Since ι maps the whole space S onto the subset S ⊆ ℝⁿ, μH[n]_{ℝⁿ}(S) = μH[n]_S(S). Together with step 3:
μH[n]_{ℝⁿ}(S) ≤ Kⁿ·μH[n]_{ℝᵖ}(f(S)).

5. Normalisation. Multiply the inequality of step 4 by c_n ≥ 0, then use (a) on ℝⁿ and on ℝᵖ with the same constant c_n:
μHE[n](S) = c_n·μH[n](S) ≤ c_n·(Kⁿ·μH[n](f(S))) = Kⁿ·(c_n·μH[n](f(S))) = Kⁿ·μHE[n](f(S)).

6. Conclusion. By (b), Lⁿ(S) = μHE[n](S), computed in ℝⁿ. Hence Lⁿ(S) ≤ Kⁿ·Hⁿ(f(S)). ∎

Remark. No measurability of S or f is used. The cases K = 0 and n = 0 need no separate treatment, because the argument is uniform. For example, for K = 0 and n ≥ 1, step 3 gives μH[n]_S(S) ≤ 0.
proof_key_steps: The restriction g = f|_S on the metric subspace S is K-anti-Lipschitz (AntilipschitzWith.of_le_mul_dist).
The anti-Lipschitz Hausdorff bound in S gives μH[n]_S(S) ≤ Kⁿ·μH[n](f(S)) (AntilipschitzWith.le_hausdorffMeasure_image, ENNReal.rpow_natCast).
The isometric inclusion S ↪ ℝⁿ gives μH[n]_S(S) = μH[n]_{ℝⁿ}(S) (Isometry.hausdorffMeasure_image, isometry_subtype_coe).
Multiplying by the common normalising constant c_n gives μHE[n](S) ≤ Kⁿ·μHE[n](f(S)) (euclideanHausdorffMeasure_def).
Since μHE[n] = volume on ℝⁿ, Lⁿ(S) ≤ Kⁿ·Hⁿ(f(S)).
